      "instructions": "Wash and dry the fresh produce.\n1 small butternut squash 2 fennel bulbs 1 small pkg fresh sage\n\nTrim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out the seeds and medium dice. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.\n\nPreheat a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat.\n\nWhile the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.\n1 medium yellow onion\n\nOnce the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and sausage; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until sausage is browned and crumbly, 5-7 minutes.\n4 tsp extra virgin olive oil 1 lb ground pork sausage\n\nMeanwhile, trim off root end and stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulbs. Halve fennel bulbs lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons.\n\nWhen the sausage is done, add fennel to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until fennel is softened and caramelized, about 5 minutes. Transfer sausage, onion, and fennel to a plate.\n\nReturn skillet to medium heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add squash and spices to the skillet. Cook, undisturbed, until the squash is just starting to brown, 2-3 minutes.\n4 tsp extra virgin olive oil 2 tsp Italian seasoning 1 tsp salt ½ tsp black pepper\n\nAdd broth to the skillet and stir to combine. Cover and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has evaporated and squash is tender, 4-5 minutes more.\n8 fl oz (1 cup) chicken or vegetable broth\n\nMeanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high and position the rack in the upper third of the oven.\n\nFinely grate Parmesan. Place in a small bowl and set aside.\n4 oz Parmesan cheese\n\nPick sage leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince half of the leaves. (Reserve remaining sage for serving.)\n\nWhen the squash is done, return sausage, onion, and fennel to the skillet along with minced sage. Stir to combine, then top with Parmesan.\n\nPlace skillet in the oven and broil until cheese is melted and golden, 3-5 minutes. Remove from oven.\n\nTo serve, divide skillet between plates or bowls.       "instructions": "Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add water and salt, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.\n1 cup jasmine rice 2 cup water ½ tsp salt\n\nMeanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.\n4 peaches 1 pint grape tomatoes 1 small pkg fresh basil\n\nOnce the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.\n\nWhile the rice is cooking, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.\n\nWhile the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels, place on a cutting board, and slice crosswise into thin strips. Season with salt and pepper.\n1 ½ lb striploin (New York strip) steak ½ tsp salt ½ tsp black pepper\n\nOnce the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add beef and stir-fry until just cooked through, 3-4 minutes. Remove to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil to keep warm. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)\n2 tsp neutral vegetable oil\n\nMeanwhile, using a clean cutting board, quarter peaches lengthwise (around the pit); twist quarters to separate, then remove and discard pits. Large dice and place in a medium bowl.\n\nHalve grape tomatoes. Add to the bowl with the peaches and set aside.\n\nPeel, halve, and medium dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.\n1 medium yellow onion 2 cloves garlic\n\nReturn skillet (with drippings) to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is starting to soften, 2-3 minutes.\n1 tbsp neutral vegetable oil ½ tsp salt ¼ tsp black pepper ¼ tsp crushed red pepper\n\nAdd peaches and tomatoes to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 5-6 minutes more. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)\n\nMeanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Place half in the reserved bowl, along with soy sauce and sugar, then whisk to combine the stir-fry sauce. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)\n¼ cup soy sauce 2 tbsp brown sugar\n\nWhen the peaches and tomatoes are softened, return steak strips (and any accumulated juices) to the skillet, then add stir-fry sauce. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until the sauce has thickened and steak is warmed through, 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat.\n\nTo serve, divide rice and stir-fry between plates or bowls.
